editorial:
Imagine the guilt you would feel if you accidentally hit a cat with your bike. That is exactly where the story starts for Allison. She thinks it is a terrible accident, but things get weird very quickly. This movie has a cool, spooky vibe that feels like those classic Saturday morning specials. It is not too scary, but it keeps you on your toes as the cat comes back time and time again. You will find yourself rooting for Allison as she tries to handle a situation that is way beyond her control.

The acting is solid for a family flick, and the pacing moves along quickly so you never get bored. While the special effects are a bit dated, they actually add to the charm of the late nineties style. If you love light horror that you can watch with your kids, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when Allison finally realizes she cannot just run away from her mistake. After the cat uses up its lives to haunt her, she has to face the ghost of the pet. Once she shows true remorse and fixes things, the cat is finally able to move on. The cycle of revenge stops, and Allison learns a big lesson about responsibility and forgiveness before the credits roll.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Goosebumps books or light spooky stories.
